verses.text: As long as an heir is a child, they're no different from a slave, even though they own everything.
They remain under guardians and managers until the date their father set.
It's the same for us: when we were children, we were enslaved to the basic principles of this world.
But when the right time came, God sent his Son, born of a woman and born under the law,
to rescue those under the law so we could be adopted as God's children.
Because you are his children, God sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, ‘Abba! Father!’
So you are no longer a slave but a child. And if you are a child, you are also an heir through God.
Before, when you didn't know God, you were enslaved to things that aren't really gods.
But now you know God—or, better, God knows you—so why are you turning back to those weak and empty principles? Do you want to be enslaved by them all over again?
You carefully observe special days, months, seasons, and years.
I'm afraid I've wasted my effort on you.
Brothers and sisters, I beg you: become like me, because I became like you. You haven't wronged me.
You know that it was because of a physical illness that I first preached the Good News to you.
Even though my condition was a trial for you, you didn't reject or despise me. You welcomed me as an angel from God—as Christ Jesus himself.
What happened to the joy you had then? I can testify that, if it had been possible, you would have torn out your eyes and given them to me.
So have I become your enemy by telling you the truth?
Those people are eager to win you over, but not for your good. They want to separate you from us so you'll be eager to follow them.
It's always good to be eager for a good purpose, not only when I'm with you.
My dear children, I'm in labor pains for you all over again until Christ is formed in you.
I wish I could be with you now and change my tone, because I don't know what to make of you.
Tell me, you who want to live under the law: do you really listen to what the law says?
Scripture says Abraham had two sons, one by a slave woman and one by a free woman.
The son of the slave woman was born in the ordinary human way, but the son of the free woman was born through God's promise.
This story can be read as an allegory: the women represent two covenants. One covenant comes from Mount Sinai and gives birth to slavery; this is Hagar.
Hagar represents Mount Sinai in Arabia and corresponds to present-day Jerusalem, which is in slavery along with her children.
But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother.

Scripture says, ‘Rejoice, you who were unable to have children and never gave birth. Break into joyful shouting, you who never had labor pains. The woman left alone will have more children than the woman with a husband.’
Brothers and sisters, you are children of the promise, like Isaac.
At that time, the son born in the ordinary human way persecuted the son born through the Spirit. It's the same now.
But what does Scripture say? ‘Send away the slave woman and her son. The slave woman's son will never share the inheritance with the free woman's son.’
So, brothers and sisters, we aren't children of the slave woman. We are children of the free woman.
